title: Followed-shell anchoring accepts `cd ABS && . script` or `cd ABS && ./x.ps1`, whose script may move the shell again
outcome: engram_shell_move reads a line that starts with `cd ABS` and changes directory nowhere else as a move TermAl follows (To). It anchors the shell at ABS once the command succeeds, even when a later command on the line sources a script (`. env.sh`, `source x`) or runs one in the shell itself (`./setup.ps1`, `call x.bat`, `Invoke-Expression`), which may change directory again. The feature doc states that a change made by a script the line runs or sources is not seen. Since PI-26a, the lost-shell reader treats such lines as hidden (anywhere), so the two paths now disagree. This predates PI-26a.
acceptance: A followed-shell move is not anchored when the rest of its line may hide a change (the lost-shell rules of engram_line_hides_changes: a sourced or in-shell script, a trap, an eval-like word, a substitution); such a line loses the shell instead, with its absolute target kept among the places; a test covers `cd /abs && . env.sh`
